@zakkster/lite-ease-params
==========================

Tunable parametric easing factories for the Lite ecosystem.
Codegen pattern: 1 allocation at factory time, 0 allocations in the hot path.
Zero dependencies, ES module, sideEffects: false, < 2 KB minified.


SHAPE
-----

Every factory returns an EasingFunction:

    EasingFunction = (t: number) => number     // t in [0, 1]

Output is in [0, 1] for Bounce. Back and Elastic can overshoot above 1 and
below 0 by design.


EXPORTS
-------

Back family (overshoot parameter, default 1.70158):
    createBackIn(overshoot?)      => (t) => y
    createBackOut(overshoot?)     => (t) => y
    createBackInOut(overshoot?)   => (t) => y

Elastic family (amplitude, period parameters; defaults 1, 0.3):
    createElasticIn(amp?, per?)      => (t) => y
    createElasticOut(amp?, per?)     => (t) => y
    createElasticInOut(amp?, per?)   => (t) => y

Bounce family (bounciness parameter, default 0.25 = Penner canonical):
    createBounceIn(bounciness?)      => (t) => y
    createBounceOut(bounciness?)     => (t) => y
    createBounceInOut(bounciness?)   => (t) => y

Type:
    EasingFunction = (t: number) => number


PARAMETER SEMANTICS
-------------------

Back.overshoot
    Penner's "back" constant. Default 1.70158 (canonical).
    Higher = deeper dip (BackIn) / bigger overshoot (BackOut).
    InOut variant internally multiplies by 1.525 per Penner.

Elastic.amplitude
    Peak overshoot magnitude. Internally clamped to >= 1.
    Reason: formula uses asin(1 / amplitude); a < 1 would be NaN.
    Default 1 reproduces Penner.

Elastic.period
    Oscillation period in t-space. Smaller = more / faster oscillations.
    Non-positive (<= 0) values fall back to 0.3.
    Default 0.3 reproduces Penner.

Bounce.bounciness
    Fraction of vertical energy retained per bounce. (0, 1).
    Internally clamped to [0.01, 0.99].
    Default 0.25 reproduces Penner exactly via a cached closure.
    Higher = more, smaller bounces. Lower = long drop, tiny final bounces.


HOT-PATH CONTRACT
-----------------

Init (factory call):
    Back:    1-2 multiplies + adds (captures overshoot, s1, possibly s).
    Elastic: 1 asin, 2 divisions (captures a, p, s, freq).
    Bounce default (0.25): 0 — returns module-level cached closure.
    Bounce parametric: 1 sqrt, ~4 mults, 5 adds (captures p1, p2, p3, n, b).

Per call:
    Back:     4 multiplies, 1 add.
    Elastic:  pow + sin + 2-4 multiplies + 1-2 adds + 0-1 branches.
    Bounce:   1-3 multiplies + 1 add + 1 branch (4 segment dispatch).
    Allocations: 0 in all cases.

Reference equality of cached default Bounce:
    createBounceOut() === createBounceOut() === createBounceOut(0.25)


MATH (BOUNCE PARAMETRIC)
------------------------

Goal: 4-segment parabolic curve, all peaks = 1, valleys = 1 - b^k.

Per-bounce velocity ratio: q = sqrt(b)   (height ratio = q^2 = b)
Half-width of bounce-k arc: h_k = q^k * p1
Gravity: n = 1 / p1^2   (so n * p1^2 = 1, peak of seg 1 reaches 1)

Constraint: segment widths sum to 1.
    p1 + 2q*p1 + 2q^2*p1 + 2q^3*p1 = 1
    p1 = 1 / (1 + 2q*(1 + q + b))    (using q^2 = b, q^3 = qb)

Breakpoints:
    p1 = 1 / (1 + 2q*(1 + q + b))
    p2 = p1 * (1 + 2q)             // p1 + 2q*p1
    p3 = p2 + 2b*p1                // p2 + 2q^2*p1
    (segment 4 implicitly ends at 1; half-width = q^3*p1 = b*sqrt(b)*p1)

Segment values (with tm = t - segment_center):
    seg 1 (t < p1):       n*t*t                       (peak 1 at t=p1)
    seg 2 (p1 ≤ t < p2):  n*tm*tm + (1 - b)           (valley 1-b)
    seg 3 (p2 ≤ t < p3):  n*tm*tm + (1 - b^2)         (valley 1-b^2)
    seg 4 (p3 ≤ t < 1):   n*tm*tm + (1 - b^3)         (valley 1-b^3)

At b = 0.25: q = 0.5, formula yields p1 = 1/2.75, matches Penner bit-exactly.


MATH (ELASTIC)
--------------

Phase shift: s = asin(1/a) * (period / (2π))     (hoisted to init)
Frequency:   freq = 2π / period                  (hoisted to init)

Out: a * pow(2, -10*t) * sin((t - s) * freq) + 1
In : -(a * pow(2, 10*(t-1)) * sin(((t-1) - s) * freq))
InOut: piecewise In on [0, 0.5], Out on (0.5, 1], scaled and offset.

a is clamped to >= 1 to keep asin(1/a) finite.
Endpoint guards: if (t === 0) return 0; if (t === 1) return 1.


MATH (BACK)
-----------

s1 = overshoot + 1

In:    t * t * (s1 * t - overshoot)
Out:   tm = t - 1; 1 + tm*tm*(s1*tm + overshoot)
InOut: s = overshoot * 1.525, s1 = s + 1
       t < 0.5: 0.5 * (4*t*t*((s1*2*t) - s))
       else:    0.5 * (tm*tm*(s1*tm + s) + 2)   where tm = 2t - 2


GUARANTEES
----------

Endpoints:
    Bounce: f(0) === 0, f(1) === 1 exactly (explicit boundary clamps).
    Back/Elastic: f(0) ≈ 0, f(1) ≈ 1 within ~2e-16 (float artifacts from
        non-exactly-representable literals like 1.70158).

InOut variants:
    f(0.5) ≈ 0.5 (within float epsilon).
    Point-symmetric around (0.5, 0.5): f(t) + f(1 - t) ≈ 1.

Bounce default:
    Bit-exact match to Penner across [0, 1] (verified at 1000-sample
    resolution: max difference = 0).


COMMON PATTERNS
---------------

1. Build at init, call in hot path.
   Build curves once at component/scene init. Don't call factories per frame.

       // GOOD
       const punch = createBackOut(2.5);
       function tick(t) { return punch(t); }

       // BAD — allocates a new closure every frame
       function tick(t) { return createBackOut(2.5)(t); }

2. ECS / SoA flyweight.
   One factory, many entities. Each entity stores only t.

       const profile = createBackOut(2.0);
       for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) {
           const t = entityT[i];
           const y = profile(t);   // shared, zero-alloc
       }

3. Bake to LUT for absolute hot-path purity.
   Pair with @zakkster/lite-ease-lut.

       import { bakeLUT, sampleLUT } from '@zakkster/lite-ease-lut';
       const LUT = bakeLUT(createElasticOut(1.3, 0.4), 256);
       // hot path: one array index instead of pow + sin

4. Compose with @zakkster/lite-ease.
   Both speak (t) => number. Mix tuned and static curves freely.

5. Use cached default for hot-path reference equality.
       const a = createBounceOut();
       const b = createBounceOut();   // a === b


PITFALLS
--------

- Calling the factory inside the hot path defeats the entire pattern.
  The factory allocates one closure; do it at init.

- Elastic.amplitude < 1 is silently clamped to 1.
  If you need "smaller" elastic, reduce period or use a different curve.

- Elastic.period <= 0 silently falls back to 0.3.

- Bounce.bounciness is clamped to [0.01, 0.99]. Out-of-range values do not
  throw; they map to the closest valid value.

- Floating-point endpoints on Back/Elastic: f(0) and f(1) may differ from
  exact 0 / 1 by ~2e-16. Use toBeCloseTo in tests, not strict equality.
  Bounce has explicit boundary clamps and is exact.


VERIFICATION
------------

The package ships with 79 tests covering:
- f(0) ≈ 0 and f(1) ≈ 1 for every factory.
- f(0.5) ≈ 0.5 for InOut variants.
- Point symmetry of InOut variants.
- Time-mirror identity: In(t) ≡ 1 - Out(1 - t).
- Default Bounce bit-exact match to Penner across [0, 1].
- Bounce parametric: continuity, peak = 1, range ⊂ [0, 1] across 9
  bounciness values.
- asin-NaN protection (amplitude < 1).
- Period fallback (period <= 0).
- Reference equality of the cached default Bounce closure.
- Determinism: same input → same output across repeated calls.
